answer:
**PCA compresses linear variance; t-SNE and UMAP emphasize neighborhood structure for a nonlinear embedding.** PCA learns a reusable linear projection. t-SNE fits coordinates to preserve selected local similarity relationships, often for visualization. UMAP also builds a neighborhood-based representation under its own objective and can support an explicit transform in common implementations. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/decomposition.html)

**Why separate t-SNE fits cannot be overlaid.** The coordinates have no shared fixed origin, rotation, or scale learned independently of each dataset. Two runs can rotate or rearrange clusters, and changes in the included points alter the optimization. A training-set point at coordinate (2,1) and a test-set point at (2,1) from a separate fit do not therefore mean the same thing.

Use a joint exploratory fit only when its transductive nature is acceptable, or a supported mapping procedure when new-point placement is needed. Do not use test-set information in a predictive pipeline while pretending the transformation was trained only on training data.

**Interpret pictures carefully.** Distances between distant t-SNE clusters, empty gaps, and cluster area need not preserve corresponding high-dimensional quantities. A beautiful separation can depend on hyperparameters and sampling. PCA's variance axes have a different, more direct linear interpretation but may miss nonlinear structure.

Evaluate embeddings according to purpose—visual exploration, compression, or prediction—and keep the preprocessing, seed, and parameters documented. A two-dimensional plot is evidence to inspect, not proof of discrete classes or model generalization.

**Technical details and references.**

PCA learns a global linear projection maximizing variance and provides a direct transform for new points. t-SNE optimizes neighborhood probability agreement in a low-dimensional layout, emphasizing local structure. UMAP builds and optimizes a neighborhood graph and commonly supports transforming new data with a fitted model. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/decomposition.html) [3](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/user_guide.html)

Independent t-SNE fits have arbitrary rotations, reflections, translations, and nonlinear layouts, so test coordinates cannot be compared with training coordinates as though they share axes. Fit a suitable joint or out-of-sample method instead, without leaking test labels into modeling decisions. Neither t-SNE distances between far clusters nor apparent cluster sizes have a simple original-space meaning. Validate representations on downstream tasks, not just attractive two-dimensional plots.
